meters.label: Searches that hit a slow shard (%)

frames.narration: A search fans out to 50 shards and waits for all 50. Each shard is slow in 1% of calls, so 1 - 0.99^50 = 39.5% of searches include at least one slow shard. We follow the call to shard 7.
The hedge logic sends the call to replica A. From its recent latency histogram it knows this shard's p95 is 13 ms, so the hedge delay is 13 ms.
At 13 ms replica A has not answered. It is in a GC pause and would take about 400 ms. Normal answers take 6 to 14 ms, so this call is in the 5% that pass the delay.
The hedge logic sends the same read to replica B on a different host. Cost: one extra request, but only about 5 in 100 calls get here.
Replica B answers in 9 ms, at about 22 ms after the first send. The first answer wins; the result arrives instead of waiting about 400 ms.
The loser is cancelled, so replica A stops the work it had not finished. Without cancellation the slow replica would keep burning CPU for the dead request.

Reads are safe to run twice. A write would need an idempotency key so the second copy does not apply again. Hedging after p50 would instead send a second request for half of all calls and could overload the shards.
